setup.pitch: Greenhollow's spring hunt begins with ninety-nine painted eggs and one First Egg meant to return last year's seed to the earth. This year the real First Egg was replaced with a jeweled replica—and sunrise has stopped at the horizon.
setup.gmSummary: Each spring Greenhollow hides ninety-nine festival eggs for children and carries one clay First Egg filled with last year's seed, ash, and a handful of new grain to the Dawn Field. The First Egg is broken into the first furrow before sunrise, symbolizing renewal and distributing a small but real agricultural enchantment. This year patron Garrick Morn replaced the humble clay egg with a jeweled replica for spectacle and had the real First Egg moved to his manor display. The dawn stalls, old roots wake beneath the meadow, and spring creatures begin protecting the unfinished cycle. The party must locate the real First Egg, learn why its contents matter, decide what belongs in the first furrow, and resolve the renewal magic by restoring the old rite, replacing it with a communal seed compact, or ending the enchantment.
setup.background: The rite began after a crop blight when Greenhollow farmers mixed surviving seed from every household into one clay egg and broke it into a shared first furrow. The magic grew around the repeated act of pooling risk and renewal. Over time, the children's hunt became the public face of the festival while the First Egg's practical purpose faded from memory. Garrick wanted a dazzling centerpiece and treated the clay egg as an ugly relic.

quest.objective: Recover the real First Egg, restore dawn, and decide how Greenhollow will begin future planting seasons.
quest.stakes: Sunrise is stalled, awakened roots are damaging the meadow, and the first planting cannot safely begin until the renewal cycle is resolved.
quest.deadline: DAWN LINE: show four sunrise marks. Fill one after meadow, egg-house, old orchard, and manor conservatory. When the fourth fills, the sun remains frozen at the horizon and the Rootwake enters the Dawn Field finale.
successConditions: The real First Egg or equivalent pooled seed reaches the Dawn Field.
The party understands that shared seed, not the shell, is the core of the rite.
The crisis ends through Restore, Replant, or Break.
failureConditions: The party abandons Greenhollow while dawn remains stalled.
The renewal magic is destroyed without securing this year's first planting seed.

facts.text: The First Egg's important contents are pooled seed and ash from Greenhollow households, not the clay shell itself.
Garrick Morn replaced the real First Egg with a jeweled replica and moved the original to his conservatory.
The rite began as a shared seed reserve after a crop failure; every household contributed so no single farm carried the risk alone.
The Rootwake is enforcing the unfinished planting cycle, not trying to destroy Greenhollow.
The crisis can end by restoring the old First Egg rite, replacing it with an explicit communal seed bank/furrow system, or breaking the enchantment and planting without magic.

scenes.title: Sunrise Stops at Gold
scenes.purpose: Launch the failed dawn rite, show the replica is functionless, and establish the sunrise clock.
scenes.readAloud: Children scatter through Greenhollow's meadow searching for painted eggs as the eastern sky turns gold. At the first-furrow marker, Garrick Morn lifts a jeweled egg above his head. The crowd cheers. He sets it into the soil—and the sun stops. Not dims. Stops. A line of roots rises behind the children like a fence.
gmNotes: Show four DAWN LINE marks. Fill 1/4 when the party leaves.
The jeweled egg can be opened or inspected immediately; it contains no seed.

DC 13 Intelligence (Nature or Investigation): success recognizes the first furrow is prepared for seed distribution, not display. Failure gives no false reading; Ina's egg-house recipe provides the same fact.
Do not run roots as an immediate combat. They herd people away from the furrow and toward safe exits.
Ina sends the party to the Egg House to compare this year's ritual materials.

scenes.title: The Egg Behind Glass
scenes.purpose: Recover the real ritual material and clarify that seed, not property ownership, is the decisive resource.
scenes.readAloud: Morn Manor's conservatory glows green beneath a glass roof. In the center, displayed on black velvet, sits a plain clay egg covered in thumbprints and old household marks. Outside the glass, roots climb the walls but do not touch the jeweled replica beside the door.
gmNotes: Fill DAWN LINE 4/4 when the real egg is opened or deliberately left under an equivalent seed plan; the finale begins immediately afterward.
Garrick can unlock the case. Otherwise DC 13 thieves' tools or Strength (Athletics) opens it; failure triggers a glass alarm and Rootbound Sprouts enter, but the case remains accessible.
Opening the clay egg does not ruin the rite. Its pooled seed can be divided or carried in another container.
If the egg is destroyed, salvage seed or substitute household contributions keep Restore/Replant available.
The Rootwake visibly reaches toward pooled seed and ignores jewels, proving its motive.

scenes.title: Return, Replant, or Sever
scenes.purpose: Resolve the spring tradition through restoration, communal replacement, or ending the enchantment.
scenes.readAloud: The sun is a bright coin balanced on the horizon. The Rootwake rises from the first furrow, taller than a cottage, crowned in unopened apple blossoms. Its hollow chest is full of dry earth. Three words split the furrow stone: RETURN. SHARE. SEVER.
gmNotes: Rootwake starts at AC 15, 82 HP.

RETURN: place pooled First Egg seed into the furrow and complete 3 Renewal actions before 2 failures using DC 13 Intelligence (Nature), Wisdom (Survival), or a concrete planting action. Failure causes a Root Surge: 1d6 bludgeoning to the actor and one failure. At 2 failures Return closes but Replant and Sever remain legal.

REPLANT: establish a seed-bank system at three stations—household contribution, emergency reserve, first-furrow distribution. Each is an Action and either automatic with recovered ledger/seed measures or DC 13 Nature/Investigation/Persuasion. Three completed stations end the crisis while replacing the egg ritual.
SEVER: target the Root Knot after one hostile action or deliberate Sever declaration. AC 14, 22 HP. Destroying it reduces Rootwake to 0 HP and permanently ends the enchantment.
Initiative 20: Root Surge. Three 10-foot squares become difficult terrain; creatures standing there make DC 13 Strength save or become Restrained until they or an ally spend an Action to free them.
Direct combat to 0 HP has the same consequence as Sever.

scenes.title: Resolution: The Egg Breaks, Spring Begins
scenes.purpose: Reward restoring the original communal act.
scenes.readAloud: The clay breaks under a hundred tiny seeds. Sunlight finally spills across the meadow. Every orchard bud opens at once—not explosively, just enough to make the children cheer. The jeweled replica remains on its stand, suddenly very obviously decoration.
gmNotes: Award 180 gp total and four Greenhollow Favor tokens.
Future festivals explain the seed-sharing purpose publicly.
The replica may remain as art but never substitutes for pooled seed.

scenes.title: Resolution: The Common Seed
scenes.purpose: Reward replacing a fragile ritual object with a durable communal system.
scenes.readAloud: Three new bins stand beside the first furrow: CONTRIBUTIONS, RESERVE, FIRST PLANTING. The Rootwake lowers its budding crown until it becomes an ordinary apple sapling rooted beside them. Sunrise moves.
gmNotes: Award 200 gp total and the Common Seed token, granting advantage on one future Greenhollow check involving farming, supplies, or mutual aid.
The egg hunt remains a celebration but no longer carries the whole agricultural system.
The seed bank includes landless workers and tenants by written rule.

scenes.title: Resolution: Spring Without a Guardian
scenes.purpose: Respect ending supernatural enforcement while preserving viable seed.
scenes.readAloud: The Root Knot splits. The Rootwake collapses into ordinary roots and wet soil. For one long moment the sun still does not move. Then Ina takes a handful of pooled seed, steps into the first furrow, and plants it by hand. Dawn continues.
gmNotes: Award 180 gp total.
The magical renewal pact ends permanently.
Greenhollow must maintain seed reserves and planting discipline without supernatural correction.

pathPressure.principle: Prepared research and shared seed make the finale safer, while rushed play retains every resolution at greater difficulty.
prepared: Old seed measures grant advantage on first Replant action.
Recovered pooled seed makes Return immediately available.
Using orchard tunnel can avoid the conservatory alarm encounter.
rushed: Skipping orchard loses old-ledger context and Replant advantage.
Breaking the display case may add Root Sprouts.
Entering without pooled seed requires gathering emergency seed from festival households before Return can begin.

cutOrder: If 25+ minutes behind, give the transfer slip and seed recipe together in the Egg House.
If 15+ minutes behind in the orchard, allow one seed offering to calm both Rootbound Hares.
Never cut the pooled-seed purpose, shared-risk history, or three final routes.
optionalOrder: Extended argument with Garrick about spectacle.
Extra egg-hunt scenes after the crisis starts.
Detailed variety names in the old seed ledger.
